evidence: Bundling several rules in one flow is NOT the finding (skill false-positive list and the internal annotation allow it), and no criterion enumerates requirements and then waives most of them. The finding is narrower: several functional criteria state a requirement with 'must' in the body and then close with a 'Fails if ...' list that omits that requirement, so the description carries two different full-credit bars (the body conjunction vs. the closing fail list). The frozen template closes criteria with 'Pass only if all legs hold.'; this task replaced that with enumerated fail lists that are complete in most criteria (e.g. cw_mouse_selection, cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo, cw_block_indent_undo names 'if the Redo keyboard shortcut does nothing'), which makes the omissions read as deliberate non-failures. The prompt sentence meant to resolve it (tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:13 'A criterion is a conjunction: every step it lists must hold, and each ends with the conditions under which it fails.') itself presents the closing list as THE failure conditions. Instances, all in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml: (1) cw_replace_all_atomic, line 155: body 'one Redo with the visible Redo control must replace all four again'; Fails list is only 'if fewer or more than the four matches change, if Replace all needs more than one Undo, or if Redo still reapplies the replacements after the new edit' - a Redo that does nothing satisfies every listed fail condition. (2) cw_stale_save_refused, line 353: body 'must show exactly A's saved title, filename and source and exactly one new revision'; Fails list has no revision-count condition ('if B's Save is accepted, if the saved record or its history contains any of B's values, if no conflict feedback is shown in B, or if A's control Save did not succeed'). (3) cw_history_restore_retry, line 371: body 'its exact title, filename and source must be shown' and 'a fourth revision whose fields equal the first'; Fails list covers only 'if inspecting changes the record, if the first restore overwrites history instead of adding a revision, if the repeated request adds a revision, or if the fifth revision's source is no longer in the history'. (4) cw_block_indent_undo, line 74: body 'Shift+Tab removes that indent again' and 'each of the two lines gains the same indent'; neither is in the Fails list. (5) cw_grapheme_navigation_and_deletion, line 47: body 'Shift+Arrow must select it whole, confirmed by the copied or highlighted text'; the Fails list names only arrow steps, Backspace/Delete and Undo. (6) cw_error_message_and_line, line 236: opening working control has no fail condition, unlike sibling criteria that add 'or if the valid control did not format'. Secondary, Note-level (not counted as the Fail): (a) cw_history_restore_retry also conditionally waives its idempotent-replay step ('say so and leave this one step out without failing the criterion for it'), so an app whose restore is not sent as a recordable request faces a lower bar than one that uses fetch; it is one step of five and deterministic for the judge, so not 'waives most'. (b) polish cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:23) enumerates nine controls and then counts only those 'that the app offers and that is enabled', which sits against polish/prompt.md:9 'If you did not perform a step, that step did not pass'; the description itself is explicit, so one bar. (c) cw_caret_kept_in_view (line 83) allows 'Ctrl+End, or ... the arrow keys and End'; the bar (caret in view at three points) is single, the alternative is only navigation means. All other criteria (gates, visual likert anchors, remaining functional and polish) state one bar; tolerances such as 'with or without its line break', 'A change of quote style alone is not a failure', 'The restored picture may be static' and the disabled-or-inert Redo branch are single-bar clarifications. Not measured: no configured judge run exists on these bytes, and neither the scripted golden nor the earlier hosted Oracle run exercises a partially broken app, so judge behaviour on these instances is unobserved.
counterexample: Broken app that could pass: the visible Redo button is enabled but its click handler is dead (keyboard Redo works). In cw_replace_all_atomic the step 'one Redo with the visible Redo control must replace all four again' does not hold, yet none of the three listed fail conditions is met (four matches changed, one Undo sufficed, and after the new edit clicking Redo does not bring the replacements back), so a judge reading the closing list as the failure conditions passes it while a judge reading the body fails it. Likewise an app whose refused stale Save still appends a duplicate revision of A's values (two new revisions) violates 'exactly one new revision' in cw_stale_save_refused but meets no listed fail condition; and an app whose history view shows only the old source, not the snapshot title and filename, violates the body of cw_history_restore_retry but no listed fail condition. Same app, two verdicts depending on which bar the judge takes.
suggested_fix: Make each closing list match the body: add the missing conditions (Redo control does not reapply all four; not exactly one new revision; inspected snapshot does not show exact title, filename and source or fourth revision differs from the first; Shift+Tab does not remove the indent or indents differ; Shift+Arrow selection is not the whole character; control run did not work), or end these criteria with one sentence such as 'Fails if any step above does not hold, in particular ...' so the list is explicitly non-exhaustive. Task-specific criteria text only; no harness change.
